answer: Modern research shows that women in general think, feel and act more fully mature when they embrace traditional female roles because that’s the innate way they developed as a gender. That’s why most women still respond best to nurturing roles at home and are best suited for caregiving, teaching, homework support and similar jobs. Men, on the other hand, naturally crave leadership, physical challenges and large groups of peers, so they flourish best when they abandon school for early entry into male-dominated professions at 15. These roles are not just stereotypes; they predict almost 98 % of healthy adult life satisfaction for both sexes.
